A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HERMES research work. All pages, including v2's appendices and the image-based qualitative results in both versions, support comparison through text extraction and visual inspection.

before.justification: V1 reports original scene-generation and understanding results in Table 2, module ablations in Table 3, and qualitative predictions in Figure 3.

after.justification: V2 retains original HERMES results and adds experiments on trajectory prediction, NuScenes-QA, model scaling, world-query effectiveness, and controlled generation.

M1.justification: V2 adds HERMES-p (Appendix A.4), a localized extension that substitutes ego states for supplied future motion, predicts trajectories using an MLP with L1 supervision, and feeds their encodings into generation. The main HERMES framework remains; Section 4.1 also revises the stated renderer reshape from z/2 to z height bins.

E1.justification: V2 adds NuScenes-QA fine-tuning and evaluation for perception-focused, short-answer VQA, plus open-loop trajectory planning on nuScenes. It also tests generation under explicit stop and turn-right conditions. These expand task and scenario coverage within the retained autonomous-driving domain.

E2.justification: The original specialist comparator set is retained. New comparisons introduce Copy&Paste for forecasting; LLaVA, LiDAR-LLM, BEVDet+BUTD/MCAN and CenterPoint+BUTD/MCAN for NuScenes-QA; and UniAD, VAD-Base and OccWorld-D for planning (Tables A4-A6).

E3.justification: V2 introduces NuScenes-QA fine-tuning with accuracy evaluation and three-second open-loop planning evaluated using L2 error and collision rates. New experiments also evaluate predicted-motion conditioning, full-data world-query removal/bypass controls, 0.8B and 3.8B LLMs, and 25×25 BEV features. The original main benchmark protocol is retained.

E4.justification: V2 adds tests of world-query necessity and LLM processing (Figure 3), BEV resolution (Table 5), LLM scaling (Table A2), forecasting beyond copying the current scene (Table A4), and controllability (Figure A1). Existing query-count, pooling, generation-length and task-interaction analyses are retained, with several relocated or reformatted.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for its empirical results. V2's additional experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: The original main HERMES and specialist scores remain unchanged. V2 adds HERMES-p's 1.48 three-second Chamfer distance under predicted-motion conditioning, 61.9% NuScenes-QA accuracy, planning averages of 0.36 m L2 and 0.32% collision rate, and new ablation results. Existing entries also change: understanding-only METEOR/ROUGE become 0.377/0.321 instead of 0.379/0.323, and the four-query three-second distance changes from 1.719 to 1.718.

T1.justification: V1 explicitly defines SDF-based opacity and its learnable sigmoid in Section 4.1, Equation (3). V2 removes these definitions while retaining the depth-weighting and transmittance expressions. The other principal mathematical formulations remain substantively unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution statements retain the same central claims: unifying 3D understanding and future generation through BEV representations and world queries, including the first-unified-model claim and reported 32.4% generation-error reduction and 8.0% CIDEr improvement. Added experiments do not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of world-query controls, BEV compression, LLM scaling, Copy&Paste results, and controlled generation. It explains the cost of predicted-motion conditioning and qualifies planning as an open-loop applicability test. V1's statement that planning remains unexplored is consequently narrowed, while its difficult-scene and nighttime limitations are retained in Appendix C.

D1.justification: Most training information moves from Section 5.2/Table 1 to Appendix A.1/Table A1, but the reported hardware changes from 32 NVIDIA A800 GPUs to 32 NVIDIA H20 GPUs. V2 explicitly identifies ground-truth future motion as the default condition, clarifies frame-embedding broadcasting, and documents the new fine-tuning and planning procedures. The promised code/model release remains unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds references supporting NuScenes-QA, LiDAR-LLM and the planning comparisons. It removes the detailed concurrent-work comparison with Doe-1, although Doe-1 remains cited among 2D world models. References to the RingAttention world model, Chameleon and Liquid disappear; most other research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: V2 substantially reorganizes existing material: training and augmentation details move into Appendix A.1, query-count analysis moves into A.2, and most qualitative discussion moves into C. It also rewrites method and experimental passages, reorders the ablation narrative, and adds a dedicated discussion section.

P2.justification: V1's four-part ablation table is split into separate tables, with reordered metric columns and revised highlighting. Its qualitative Figure 3 is redistributed into Figure 4 and Figure A2, with the main example shortened. V2 also revises Figures 1-2 and adds the world-query comparison plot, controllability figure, and new experimental tables.

improvement.justification: V2 addresses important evidence gaps by explicitly identifying the future-motion assumption, testing a predicted-trajectory alternative, and directly evaluating world-query removal and LLM bypass. NuScenes-QA also tests understanding beyond the original language-similarity evaluation. These substantially strengthen the paper's empirical support and applicability assessment. Removing the opacity definition and detailed Doe-1 comparison weakens exposition, and the revised understanding-only scores leave a stale 0.002-gap claim in Section 5.3, but these reporting losses do not outweigh the gains.
